evidence.snippet: Chinese gold imports rose 39.3% year-on-year to 141.7 tonnes in August, taking year-to-date imports to a record 1,141.2 tonnes, up 72.2%. Lower gold prices, a stronger yuan and persistent domestic price premiums encouraged inflows, while banks also drew on remaining import quotas under the licensing regime introduced by the People's Bank of China in June. Chinese gold ETFs added around 44 tonnes through August, an 18% increase from the start of the year, according to the Shanghai Gold Exchange, while global ETF holdings were broadly unchanged. LME copper extended gains for a sixth consecutive session on Tuesday, its longest winning streak since May, before retreating slightly Wednesday morning, as tight physical market conditions in China continued to support prices. Falling inventories, holiday-related restocking and seasonal demand ahead of the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays boosted consumption. Shanghai copper cathode inventories fell by 14,700 tonnes to 43,900 tonnes, the lowest level since December 2023. While imported copper arrivals have increased, most material has flowed directly to fabricators rather than warehouses, keeping spot supplies tight. Indonesia's Morowali Industrial Park (IMIP) has instructed nickel pig iron producers to curb output as El Niño-related drought conditions strain water supplies needed for processing operations. The cuts could affect around 100,000 tonnes of NPI production, compared with the park's annual capacity of roughly 4.2 million tonnes. Investor positioning across base metals remained subdued. According to the latest COTR data, net bullish copper positions fell by 3,981 lots to 42,132 lots, the lowest level since late March and marking a sixth consecutive weekly decline despite higher prices. evidence.snippet: Central bank rate hikes in the past two weeks have not daunted investors. First, Saudi Arabia is restarting its East-West pipeline, which bypasses the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi Arabia expects the pipeline to be at 40% of its capacity in the coming days. A full restart will take 6-8 weeks. Second, hopes are rising of a diplomatic end to the US-lran war as diplomatic efforts pick up around the UN General Assembly (UNGA). President Donald Trump said he is "probably" open to a meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, on the sidelines of the UNGA. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have already met with an Iranian delegation, and the US administration described the meeting as going "very well" and pointed to the possibility of another meeting in the “very near future." The UNGA could disappoint investors, however. Currently, there is no meeting scheduled between Trump and Pezeshkian. Trump also continues threatening to annihilate Iran unless a deal is done, a tactic that has failed to move the Iranians in the past. items.original_title: FinancialJuice: Chip Rally Drives Nasdaq 100 to Record as Oil Falls – US Market Wrap

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: Chip Rally Drives Nasdaq 100 to Record as Oil Falls – US Market Wrap
evidence.snippet: A renewed rally in chipmakers pushed the Nasdaq 100 to its first record since June, while sentiment was also supported by falling oil prices amid hopes for diplomatic efforts to end the Iran war. The tech-heavy index rose 0.8%. A closely watched gauge of semiconductor giants including Micron Technology and Nvidia advanced for a sixth consecutive session. Gains in chipmakers offset a selloff in bank shares. Brent crude settled around $99 after President Donald Trump said US officials held a “very good” meeting with Iranian envoys in New York. Bonds stabilized. Trump said the three-hour meeting, held on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, was “very productive” and that another meeting was being planned for the near future. He added there was “a lot of momentum” toward a deal with Iran as White House advisers Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with mediators. The US administration has signaled a renewed push to bring the war in the Middle East to an end, with Trump claiming in his speech that the conflict will conclude shortly after the November midterm elections. Wall Street is also preparing for this week’s summit between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, giving the leaders of the world’s two largest economies an opportunity to strengthen personal ties and seek common ground on contentious issues.
